triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '5. @cute.jit helper scoping has ZERO effect on register pressure' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 5. @cute.jit helper scoping has ZERO effect on register pressure

problem.statement: GDN Chunk Forward Pitfalls (CuTeDSL, SM120) -- 5. @cute.jit helper scoping has ZERO effect on register pressure

payload.attempted: You factor accumulator-heavy code into `@cute.jit` helper functions, expecting the compiler to limit accumulator live ranges to the helper's scope.
payload.lesson: Don't waste time refactoring for register relief via helpers. The only ways to reduce register pressure in CuTeDSL are: (a) reduce algorithmic live values, (b) reduce tile sizes, (c) SMEM stride padding to reduce bank conflicts (which reduces spill cycles, not register count).

established_fact.mechanism: `@cute.jit` functions are always inlined before LLVM live-range analysis. The compiler sees one flat function body regardless of source-level scoping. Python-level function boundaries have no effect on register allocation.

payload.observed: No change in register count or spill traffic. Measured across three independent attempts (V5a, V9, V12a of the broader DeltaNet optimization campaign).
payload.root_cause: `@cute.jit` functions are always inlined before LLVM live-range analysis. The compiler sees one flat function body regardless of source-level scoping. Python-level function boundaries have no effect on register allocation.
